messages:
nightly-bot: [ALERT] nightly-rag-eval failed — recall drop ~11% on 'sme_docs' promptset. run_id=nightly/1971203456. rerank-pass loss spiked.
devon: saw this in dashboard. Anyone triaging? Looks like topk recall shifted a lot for a small set of queries.
maya: I'm on it. quick thought: kv-cache prefill rollout went live yesterday; could that change inputs fed to the embedder (truncation/offsets)? reranker uses embeddings, not token positions, but input differences matter.🔍 andre: embedding pipeline had a config drift too — embed-pipeline v3.2.4 deployed at 03:12 (PR #412). there was an unintentional toggle: use_8bit=true for a subset. checking index metadata now.
lina: pulled 10 failing queries. before recall topk ids for q_1423 were [d9,d2,d5]; after they're [d2,d9,d7]. reranker scores: before [0.92,0.88,0.73], after [0.85,0.84,0.68] — overall shift down.
--- logs snippet ---
```
$ grep "q_1423" rerank_outputs.log
q_1423 BEFORE: d9:0.92 d2:0.88 d5:0.73
q_1423 AFTER:  d2:0.85 d9:0.84 d7:0.68
```
devon: did a quick vector diff for same docs across runs. l2 diffs mostly ~0.02-0.05, but a handful >0.2 which explains reordering. the >0.2 ones correlate with docs that hit a special tokenization path (quoted blocks) and might be affected by prefill.
maya: can you dump the encoder inputs (post-tokenizer) for one affected doc+query pair? also confirm model variants used in nightlies: reranker=rnr-v2-quant, embed=embed-instr-1b-8bit? andre: confirm: nightly metadata shows reranker=rnr-v2-quant, embed=embed-instr-1b-8bit, KV_PREFILL=true. i kicked a staging eval with EMBED_PIPELINE=v3.2.3 and KV_PREFILL=false. preliminary: recall matches baseline.
lina: quick repro steps I ran:
```
# baseline setup
EMBED_PIPELINE=v3.2.3 KV_PREFILL=false ./run_nightly_eval --dataset sme_docs
# suspect setup
EMBED_PIPELINE=v3.2.4 KV_PREFILL=true ./run_nightly_eval --dataset sme_docs
```
Result: baseline ~orig recall, suspect run reproduces ~11% drop. so interaction between embed-pipeline change and kv prefill seems likely.
devon: ok actionable hypothesis: either v3.2.4 changed tokenization/normalization OR 8-bit quantization introduces vector drift amplified by prefill path differences.
maya: action items: 1) andre roll back embed-pipeline to v3.2.3 on staging and run full nightly (andre). 2) i'll add a unit/eval that asserts tokenizer parity between prefill and non-prefill paths + add a regression test comparing encoder inputs (maya). 3) lina add a focused eval that computes per-doc l2 diffs and flags >0.1 (lina).
andre: rolled back staging to v3.2.3, kicked eval. initial metrics look back to baseline. opened ticket ML-8342 with logs/samples: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-8342
maya: assigning ML-8342 to @maya, i'll push tokenizer parity test by EOD and a patch to ensure prefill uses identical truncation rules. tagging ops to hold kvcache-prefill rollout.
ops-bot: KV_PREFILL rollout paused in prod :warning: (ticket ML-8342).
devon: thanks. after tests land let's run incremental canary with a limited traffic slice. follow-up sync tomorrow morning if needed.
note: thread contains short messages, code snippets, and action items consistent with Slack style
